veranderings.voor: Die provinsies se wetgewers stuur die Raad se lede.
veranderings.na: Die wetgewers van die provinsies stuur die lede van die Raad.
veranderings.rede: Two stacked 'se' possessives in one short sentence read clumsily; the 'van' form is clearer and keeps the meaning.

veranderings.voor: waar die lede dit bespreek en dikwels verander
veranderings.na: waar die lede hulle bespreek en dikwels verander
veranderings.rede: The pronoun refers back to the plural 'Die meeste voorstelle', so it should be 'hulle', not 'dit'.
The block refers to the proposal as 'dit' everywhere else and uses 'hy' for the President in the next sentences, so 'hy' here is confusing; 'daar' points back to the other house.
Two sentences earlier the President must 'onderteken'; using the same verb avoids suggesting a different act.

veranderings.blok: Waarom reëls en wette saak maak
veranderings.voor: op 'n slag en die ander luister
veranderings.na: op 'n slag, en die ander luister
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.

veranderings.blok: Waarom reëls en wette saak maak
veranderings.voor: praat baie mense gelyk en is dit moeilik
veranderings.na: praat baie mense tegelyk, en is dit moeilik
veranderings.rede: 'tegelyk' is the standard word for 'at the same time' and avoids confusion with 'gelyk' meaning equal, which this lesson uses in its equality block; the AWS comma goes before 'en' joining two clauses.

veranderings.voor: gee hulle die saak aan 'n staatsaanklaer
veranderings.na: gee hulle die saak oor aan 'n staatsaanklaer
veranderings.rede: Handing a case on is idiomatically 'oorgee aan'; 'gee die saak aan' reads like an anglicism of 'give the case to'.
Repeating the protected office name keeps the term consistent, since 'aanklaer' alone can be confused with a complainant.

veranderings.voor: bekende mense en mense wat niemand ken.
veranderings.rede: The clause lacks the closing 'nie' required after 'niemand', and 'mense wat niemand ken' can also mean people who know nobody; 'onbekende mense' fixes both and mirrors 'bekende mense'.
'waar' reads as a place or as referring to 'mense'; 'waarin' ties the clause to 'geskille'.
